summary: High on a limestone ridge overlooking the valley, Cyrus adjusts the heavy tripod of a long-range thermal scanner, his gloved hands moving with clinical precision. He looks through the eyepiece, his eye-line shifting as he tracks the heat signatures of the nomadic fleet moving through the shimmering heat haze miles below. He reaches down to pick up a smooth, black stone, rolling it between his thumb and forefinger while his gaze remains fixed on the distant dust clouds raised by Arvin’s lead tanker. "The more they build, the more debris I have to scrub from my sky," Cyrus whispers to the empty desert wind.

summary: Milo and Arvin struggle to hoist a heavy, corrugated heat shield onto the side of the makeshift rocket frame in the center of the camp. Milo grunts as he pushes the jagged metal plate into position, his boots slipping on the loose gravel of the launchpad while Arvin leans his shoulder against the hot metal to brace it. They work in tandem, the physical strain visible in the cords of their necks as they fight the awkward weight of the recycled armor against the wind. "Hold it steady or the vibration will tear the whole fuselage apart," Milo says through his grit-clenched teeth.
settingText: The background is filled with the low-tech clutter of the Launch-Shop, including hanging copper coils, stacks of lead-acid batteries, and a flickering halogen work light that casts long, shaky shadows across the corrugated metal walls of the converted tanker. A layer of fine Mojave sand crunches underfoot whenever someone moves.
